title: Shared ground: Roman and Protestant doctors agree the living faithful can and ought to trust their reconciliation
source_text: XXX. Porro ex iis quae a nobis tum in hac disputatione, tum in praecedenti exposita sunt patet, inter Theologos Ecclesiae Romanae & Protestantes quaestionem non esse, An fideles per Christi gratiam justificati adeo possint, & debeant firmiter esse persuasi, & suae cum Deo reconciliationis certam habere fiduciam; quandoquidem, jam ostendimus, communi cum Protestantibus consensu, id fateri Doctores Scholae Romanae: quorum aperta doctrina est eos qui viva fide in Christum praediti sunt, non tantum posse, sed etiam debere, de remissione peccatorum suorum, & sua apud Deum justitia confidere, & certam habere persuasionem.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover from those things which have been set out by us both in this disputation and in the preceding it is plain that between the theologians of the Roman Church and the Protestants the question is not whether the faithful justified by Christ’s grace can and ought to be so firmly persuaded and to have a certain trust of their reconciliation with God; since, as we have already shown, by common consent with the Protestants the doctors of the Roman School confess that: whose open doctrine is that those who are endowed with a living faith in Christ not only can but also ought to trust concerning the remission of their sins and their righteousness with God, and to have a certain persuasion.
pass_b_english: On Le Blanc’s reading the live dispute is not whether justified believers may firmly trust their reconciliation.
Roman doctors openly teach that living faith both can and ought to yield certain persuasion of pardon—common ground with Protestants.

rejected: there is no issue at all
